clue.text: Sweeney Todd's customer was so distressed

definitions.meaning: the demon barber slashed his customers with a razor, so each one was literally slashed to pieces
upset, badly shaken by bad news

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the literal fate of the barber's victims, sliced open, and the idiom for being emotionally upset.

clue.text: Box-maker joins eccentric governing body

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
a board governs a company or institution

explanation.surface: An odd character joins a company's board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like an anagram signal but means a card, an odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff pasteboard is the material from which boxes are made.

clue.text: Instruct church to support temperance beverage

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes underneath, so this one comes second

parts.note: tea is the drink of those who abstain from alcohol

explanation.surface: Clergy are told to back the teetotal drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temperance' refers to abstaining from alcohol, so the beverage is TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone is to give them lessons.

clue.text: Young Indian's pretence about a postal order

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads as 'a young Indian is'

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: a pose is an affected pretence

explanation.surface: A Native American feigns interest in a money order.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the Algonquian term for a Native American baby or the carrier it is held in.

clue.text: Drug of no avail after Macbeth's murder

definitions.text: Drug of no avail after Macbeth's murder

parts.words: Drug of no avail after Macbeth's murder
parts.note: Macbeth is told he 'does murder sleep', so once sleep itself is killed, a sleeping draught has nothing left to work on

explanation.surface: A poison or remedy proves useless once Macbeth has done his killing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line from the play is 'Macbeth does murder sleep': the 'murder' is of sleep, not of Duncan, so the drug in question is one that induces sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleep-inducing drug is a narcotic or sedative, which would be pointless once slumber has been destroyed.

clue.text: Ghost had to appear in The Empress of Blandings

indicators.note: one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: in P. G. Wodehouse's stories the Empress of Blandings is Lord Emsworth's prize pig, a sow

explanation.surface: A spirit turned up in a Wodehouse tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The Empress sounds like a royal lady but is Wodehouse's champion pig, so she is a SOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade or spectre is a ghost, as in the shadows of the dead.

clue.text: Financial record shows no bid over reserve

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece above comes first

parts.note: in bridge a player who makes no bid says pass
to reserve a seat is to book it

explanation.surface: An auction ends with no bids above the reserve price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no bid' and 'reserve' suggest an auction; they come from bridge and booking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank book records the deposits and withdrawals on an account.

clue.text: Make good waste, replacing right eye - £200

indicators.note: the letters are placed anew, in a different order

parts.note: £ is L (from libra, the pound), and 200 in Roman numerals is CC

explanation.surface: A surgeon swaps out someone's right eye for two hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges R, EYE, L and CC. The pound sign stands for L because it comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprocess discarded material is to turn rubbish into something useful.

clue.text: Three notes to start the blues and give us the works

indicators.note: these notes come at the beginning, before the next piece

parts.note: F, A and C are musical notes
blue is the colour of the Conservative Party, whose members are Tories

explanation.surface: A musician plays three notes to open a blues number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the blues' sounds like music but means Tories, as blue is the Conservative colour in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Works in the sense of industrial plants are manufacturing buildings.

clue.text: Expert's witticism

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means first-rate, as in a ... shot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both highly skilled, as in elite troops, and a sharp joking remark.

clue.text: Is seen again to harvest fruit

parts.note: to harvest a crop is to reap it
pears are a kind of fruit

explanation.surface: A farmer watches a crop return each year, ready to be gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into view is to show up again after an absence.

clue.text: Officers meet to have a drink

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer; two officers give two of them
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer; two officers give two of them

explanation.surface: Senior officers gather in the mess for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officers' is plural, so it supplies two COs side by side; 'meet to have' only joins them to the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from cacao powder is a common bedtime drink.

clue.text: Somehow emerging, avoiding pirate (or perhaps shark)

parts.note: to get by something is to pass and avoid it, so 'by' stands for avoiding; it is used for both halves
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan
taken as written
to get by something is to pass and avoid it, so 'by' stands for avoiding; it is used for both halves
a shark is a swindler, a crook

explanation.surface: Someone escapes, giving a pirate or perhaps a shark the slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shark' looks like a fish but means a swindler; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by any means available, fair or foul, which is how something gets done somehow.

clue.text: Comparatively roguish radio character?

definitions.meaning: arch means playfully roguish, so the comparative form means more roguish
the long-running BBC radio soap The ... is about a farming family of that name, so any of them is a radio character

explanation.definitionFit: Arch (cheekily mischievous) takes -er for its comparative, and the same spelling is the surname of the farming family in Britain's oldest radio soap.

clue.text: Customers elect perhaps? That's about right

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other piece
perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Customers may choose, but the trader stays in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals a rearrangement of the clue's 'elect' (giving CTELE), and 'about' wraps that round the right. A lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid; 'That's' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's patrons, taken together, are its body of customers.

clue.text: A parakeet rather than a duck

definitions.text: A parakeet rather than a duck

parts.words: A parakeet rather than a duck
parts.note: a duck is a nil score in cricket, the same as nil in tennis, so the small parrot is a zero-score bird rather than a duck

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher identifies a small parrot, not a waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, and in tennis nought is called 'love'; so the parrot is a 'nought bird' as opposed to the waterfowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Small African parrots of the genus Agapornis, often kept in pairs, go by this affectionate name.

clue.text: These stud adjustments used to protect furniture

indicators.note: adjusting the letters reshapes these words

explanation.surface: Fitted studs are altered to protect furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth spread over furniture keeps off dust when a room is not in use.

clue.text: Like the continuing storm when a French boy accepts a degree

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: un is French for a
Ted is a boy's name
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A French lad gets his degree while a storm rages on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts the second 'a' plus the degree inside the French article plus the boy, splitting them. 'when' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm that goes on without lessening has not died down at all.

clue.text: Old copper top-hole — but the tap's so faulty

parts.note: D stood for the old British penny, a copper coin, before decimal currency in 1971
top-hole and ripping are both old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: An elderly policeman says things are splendid, though the tap is leaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old copper' suggests a retired policeman, but it is the pre-1971 British penny, abbreviated D.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty tap leaks water drop by drop, so it is leaking in that way.

clue.text: Exact summary before mid- September

parts.note: a précis is a summary

indicators.note: the middle letter of the nine-letter month

explanation.surface: A precise summary is due by mid-September.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise means accurate and exact.

clue.text: Official procedure for the pop establishment

definitions.text: Official procedure for the pop establishment

parts.words: Official procedure for the pop establishment
parts.note: pop is short for population, and the official procedure establishes how many people there are, not anything to do with pop music

explanation.surface: Some formal process governs the pop-music business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop establishment' reads as the music industry, but pop means population and establish means determine.
explanation.definitionFit: A government head-count records the number and details of everyone living in a country.

clue.text: Beg for quarters with free entertainment

parts.note: E and N are compass points, quarters of the compass
a treat is something given for nothing

explanation.surface: People beg for lodgings along with free shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead earnestly is to beg.

clue.text: Woman, originally retired, becomes corrupted

annotationWithheld.why: Woman, originally retired, becomes corrupted (6): the only parse is RIB (woman as originally made, from Adam's rib) inside BED, with 'retired' giving both BED and the containment, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Diversions for travellers in Kent

parts.note: the travellers are Chaucer's pilgrims riding to the cathedral city in Kent, and the diversions are the stories they tell to pass the time

explanation.surface: Road closures send motorists in Kent on detours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversions' suggests road detours; here it means entertainments. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's fourteenth-century poem is a sequence of stories told by pilgrims for amusement on the road.

clue.text: Capital return in winning Victoria Cross

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A capital city welcomes back a hero who won the Victoria Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads ORIAC, from victORIA Cross, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian capital is this city on the Nile.

clue.text: "Summer's — hath all too short a date" (Shakespeare)

definitions.text: "Summer's — hath all too short a date" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "Summer's — hath all too short a date" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: the gap is the missing word in Sonnet 18, where summer's term of tenure runs out too soon

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's sonnet with one word blanked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy agreement grants use for a fixed period, which summer's term is in the sonnet.

clue.text: From Venice, nine subjects of a warrior queen

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Nine Venetians are the subjects of some warrior queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The warrior queen is Boudicca, who led the tribe in revolt against Roman Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca ruled this ancient British tribe of East Anglia, so its people were her subjects.

clue.text: Description of seamen in troubled water — all things needed on board

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, as the seamen are inside the water
troubled water is churned up, so the word water is rearranged

parts.note: able is the word in 'able seamen', describing a qualified sailor

explanation.surface: Sailors in rough seas need everything carried on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the clue's 'water' to TWARE, and 'in' puts the seamen's description inside it. 'Board' looks like a ship's deck but is a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cutlery and glasses are what you need to lay a table, the board.

clue.text: Enclose object found in dictionary but not closely defined

indicators.note: these words say one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
to pen something is to enclose it
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Someone looks up a word in the dictionary but finds its meaning vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no fixed limits is loose and unrestricted, never pinned down precisely.

clue.text: Gold taken from turbulent flow of the river

indicators.note: one word is removed out of another

parts.note: a torrent is a violent, rushing stream
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold is panned out of the river's rushing water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands, flowing into the Humber.
